resources.string: End-to-end encrypted. Peer-to-peer over Tor.\nNo phone number. No email. No server.
Pick a name for yourself. It is only a local label — nothing is registered anywhere.
A cryptographic key will be generated and stored on this device only.
Let a contact scan this to add you
No contacts yet.\n\nTap “My code” to show your pairing QR, or “Add contact” to scan someone else’s.
That QR is not a LegendMessage contact code
%1$s was added. Your messages will be end-to-end encrypted. For both of you to message each other, they need to add you too.
Tor route not published yet — start Tor on the home screen
To stay reachable, LegendMessage needs to be exempt from battery optimization. Open settings to allow it?
%1$s\n\nCompare these digits with your contact in person or over another trusted channel. If they match on both devices, no one is intercepting your conversation.
Not available yet — pair with this contact first.
Back up your identity and contacts to an encrypted file, so you can restore them on another device. Your message history is not included.
The backup is encrypted with the passphrase you choose. If you lose the passphrase, the backup cannot be recovered.
This passphrase encrypts (or decrypts) the backup file. Choose something strong you will remember.
Identity restored. Please restart the app.

Without a mailbox, you and a contact must be online at the same time. A mailbox is another always-on device running this app in mailbox mode; it holds encrypted messages for you until you pick them up. It only ever sees ciphertext.
Your mailbox address (where your messages wait for you)
Mailbox saved. Share your code again so contacts pick up the change.
Run this device as a mailbox for my contacts
This device\'s address (use it as a mailbox on your other device):
Not available yet — wait for Tor to come online.
Refuse to send messages to a contact until you have compared and confirmed their safety number.
⚠ Unverified — tap to compare the safety number and verify this contact.
✓ You have marked this contact verified.
Not yet verified. Compare these digits with %1$s over a trusted channel, then mark verified.
Verified-only sending is on. Compare %1$s\'s safety number and mark them verified before messaging.
You already have a contact named \"%1$s\" with a different key. This could be an innocent name clash — or someone impersonating them. Only add if you trust this code.
Hides your onion service from anyone who hasn\'t been authorized with a key from your contact code. EXPERIMENTAL and untested on-device — leave off unless you can test messaging on two devices.

Experimental. For this to work, you and your contacts must re-share and re-scan your codes (so client-auth keys are exchanged), then restart Tor. If messaging stops working, turn this back off and restart Tor.
Remove the PIN lock? The app will open without asking for a PIN.
The PIN gates the app and your history. The Tor service keeps running while locked, so messages still arrive. If you forget the PIN there is no recovery except erasing and restoring from a backup.
Choose a PIN to unlock the app. At least 4 digits.
There is no way to recover a forgotten PIN. You can erase this device\'s identity and history and start over (or restore from a backup). Erase now?
Permanently erase this device\'s identity, keys, contacts, and all message history. There is no undo and no server copy. Use this if the device may fall into the wrong hands.
This wipes your identity, contacts, and message history for good. To confirm, type ERASE below.
